sources.title: ADR-004: Distributed Cache Layer Evaluation (Redis vs Memcached)
sources.author: Elena Rostova (Principal Architect)
sources.reason: Redis provides sub-2ms p99 response times under 25k req/sec, rich native data structures for tagging, RDB/AOF persistence against cold-start thundering herds, and Pub/Sub invalidation.
sources.rejected: Memcached rejected due to lack of persistence snapshots and missing pub/sub cache invalidation channels.

sources.title: ADR-002: Primary Store Selection (PostgreSQL vs MongoDB)
sources.author: Elena Rostova (Principal Architect)
sources.reason: Strict ACID guarantees and declarative foreign key cascades needed for multi-tenant billing ledger integrity and SOC2 audit compliance.
sources.rejected: MongoDB rejected due to weak distributed cross-collection transactional guarantees and absence of referential constraint enforcement.

sources.title: ADR-007: Authentication Strategy (Stateless JWT vs Redis Session Store)
sources.author: David Patel (Security Lead)
sources.decision: Adopt Opaque Session Tokens in Redis
sources.reason: Allows instant session revocation upon logout, password reset, or privilege revocation in <2ms, satisfying enterprise SSO security criteria.
sources.rejected: Stateless JWT rejected because compromised tokens remain valid until expiration without maintaining a centralized revocation list anyway.

sources.title: ADR-011: Dashboard API Gateway (GraphQL Federation vs REST)
sources.author: Marcus Chen (Lead Backend Engineer)
sources.decision: Adopt GraphQL Aggregation Layer for Web/Mobile Clients
sources.reason: Consolidates 12 sequential REST roundtrips into 1 HTTP POST, slashes network payload by 68%, and drops mobile dashboard render times from 3.2s to 640ms.
sources.rejected: Bespoke composite REST endpoints rejected due to tight backend-frontend coupling and slow iteration cycles.

sources.title: ADR-009: Asynchronous Message Broker (RabbitMQ vs Apache Kafka)
sources.author: Elena Rostova (Principal Architect)
sources.reason: Native support for per-message acknowledgments, dead-letter exchanges (DLX) for retry backoffs, and priority queues at low operational overhead for 5,000 msg/sec.
sources.rejected: Apache Kafka rejected due to operational complexity of ZooKeeper/KRaft clusters, lack of individual message ACK/retry semantics, and overhead for discrete task queues.
